subject: rstan does not find StanHeaders' libraries on multiple architectures (linux) installations

messages.author: 6cd426f33f0a8492
messages.subject: rstan does not find StanHeaders' libraries on multiple architectures (linux) installations
parts:
Dear all,

Presumably, this should/could have been reported much earlier, but I must admit that the last months I had no need to compile a Stan program on my machine.  I was using mostly another machine which has a binary distribution of R installed.  But that machine is currently down and so I had to use my own machine on which R is installed from source, both as a 32-bit architecture and a 64-bit architecture.

To my surprise, compilation failed.  The error message was, essentially:

   /usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lStanHeaders
   collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status

So I thought the problem might be related to Dieter Menne's "Error installing 2.13 on Windows" report, but perhaps not.

My machine is:

    berwin@ECM-DTC-716:~$ uname -a
    Linux ECM-DTC-716 4.4.0-57-generic #78-Ubuntu SMP Fri Dec 9 23:50:32 UTC 2016 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

And I received the above error message with R 3.3.2, rstan 2.14.1 and StanHeaders 2.14.0 as well with R 3.3.1, rstan 2.12.1 and StanHeaders 2.12.0. (The only two R installations on my machine that have rstan and StanHeaders installed.)

I followed the suggestions in the thread started by Dieter Menne, removing and re-installing StanHeaders and rstan multiple times.  Finally I realised that the stan() command had a "verbose=TRUE" option.  Once I used this, I could spot the problem immediately (slowly stopping kicking myself for not realising this earlier :) ).  See the two attached files which try to compile the school example from rstan's vignette on my machine, once using the 32-bit version and once the 64 bit version.  Both files state:

    >> setting environment variables: 
    PKG_LIBS =  -L'/opt/R/R-3.3.2/lib/R/library/StanHeaders/lib' -lStanHeaders

and these values are later used in a "g++ -shared" (or "g++ -m32 -shared") command.  But on my machine:

    berwin@ECM-DTC-716:~$ locate libStanHeaders
    /opt/R/R-3.3.1/lib/R/library/StanHeaders/lib/32/libStanHeaders.a
    /opt/R/R-3.3.1/lib/R/library/StanHeaders/lib/64/libStanHeaders.a
    /opt/R/R-3.3.2/lib/R/library/StanHeaders/lib/32/libStanHeaders.a
    /opt/R/R-3.3.2/lib/R/library/StanHeaders/lib/64/libStanHeaders.a

So it is no surprise that the linker cannot find the StanHeaders library.

I guess a fix for the moment is to link "/opt/R/R-3.3.2/lib/R/library/StanHeaders/lib/64/libStanHeaders.a" to "/opt/R/R-3.3.2/lib/R/library/StanHeaders/lib/libStanHeaders.a" and not use rstan with the 32 bit architecture.

The only place in rstan's sources that I could find that seem to relate to the above output of environment variables is in the function 'rstanplugin' defined in "plugin.R":

    if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows")
      StanHeaders_pkg_libs <- system.file("libs", .Platform$r_arch, package = "StanHeaders")
    else StanHeaders_pkg_libs <- system.file("lib", package = "StanHeaders")

I must admit that I am a bit puzzled by this code.  Why is the architecture only taken into account if R is run on a Windows platform?

Wishing you all a Happy New Year! 

Cheers,

Berwin

    else StanHeaders_pkg_libs <- system.file("lib", package = "StanHeaders")

I must admit that I am a bit puzzled by this code.  Why is the architecture only taken into account if R is run on a Windows platform?

I just didn't anticipate anyone trying to compile R and Stan programs in 32 bit mode on a non-Windows machine.

Sooner or later there is always the odd one. :)   But I believe there are actually quite a few people who run two architectures on linux, otherwise the manual would not discuss it is such details.  Brian (Ripley) definitely has 32 and 64 architectures installed. :)  I am perhaps a bit unusual in that I install both builts as sub-architectures....

So, for you
      .Platform$r_arch
comes up as 32 or 64 depending on which version you run?

Yes (as character strings).
As I understand from 'help(.Platform)':

    r_arch: character string, possibly '""'.  The name of an 
                architecture-specific directory used in this build of R.

Thus, I would have thought that regardless of platform, a simple

would suffice to locate the correct directory in which StanHeaders' libraries are installed.

Cheers,
Berwin
